skill.name: c-pro

content.value_statement: C projects often fail through memory leaks, unchecked system calls, and fragile build practices. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward safer systems code, focused tests, and practical verification.
actual_capabilities: Plans C implementations around explicit memory ownership and allocation checks.
Reviews pointer arithmetic, data structures, and resource lifetime risks.
Guides POSIX system call usage with consistent error handling.
Adapts designs for embedded constraints and limited stack usage.
Suggests pthreads patterns, debugging steps, and profiling workflows.
Produces guidance for Makefiles, headers, unit tests, and benchmarks.
limitations: It does not compile, run, or verify code unless the host environment provides tools.
It cannot prove memory safety without tests, sanitizers, or runtime evidence.
It provides C99/C11 guidance, not certification for safety critical systems.
It may need project specific hardware details for embedded recommendations.

use_cases.title: Systems Developer Code Review
use_cases.description: Review a C module for ownership, POSIX error handling, and benchmark readiness before merging.

use_cases.title: Embedded Firmware Planning
use_cases.description: Plan data structures and stack usage for firmware with tight memory and processor limits.

use_cases.title: Engineering Lead Quality Checklist
use_cases.description: Create a practical review checklist for C reliability, tests, debugging, and maintainability.

prompt_templates.title: Review Basic Memory Safety
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this C function for memory ownership, null checks, and return value handling. Explain the highest risk issues first.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one function or small module

prompt_templates.title: Design a Safe Data Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a C data structure for this workload. Include ownership rules, allocation strategy, error handling, and test cases.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for maintainable C components

prompt_templates.title: Audit POSIX and Threading Risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this POSIX C module for system call failures, signal safety concerns, pthreads issues, and portability problems.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of system programming code

prompt_templates.title: Optimize with Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Optimize this performance critical C path. Start with profiling assumptions, identify safe changes, and define benchmarks that prove improvement.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced performance work with measurable results

output_examples.input: Review a C parser that allocates buffers and returns error codes.
output_examples.output: A prioritized review noting missing allocation checks, unclear buffer ownership, and suggested tests for malformed input.

output_examples.input: Plan an embedded ring buffer for sensor readings.
output_examples.output: A design outline with fixed capacity storage, ownership rules, overflow behavior, and validation tests for memory limits.

output_examples.input: Improve a POSIX file copy utility.
output_examples.output: A checklist covering partial reads and writes, errno handling, cleanup paths, and benchmark measurements.

best_practices: State ownership for every allocated object and define who frees it.
Check every allocation and system call before using returned values.
Profile before optimizing and measure changes with repeatable benchmarks.
anti_patterns: Skipping cleanup paths because an error appears rare.
Using pointer arithmetic without bounds or lifetime notes.
Optimizing before tests, profiling, and correctness checks exist.

faq.question: Does this skill write C code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help draft C code, headers, Makefiles, tests, and review notes.

faq.question: Which C standards does it target?
faq.answer: It focuses on C99 and C11 guidance, with POSIX practices where relevant.

faq.question: Can it find memory leaks?
faq.answer: It can identify likely leak paths and recommend Valgrind or sanitizer checks.

faq.question: Is it suitable for embedded systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It considers stack usage, allocation limits, and resource constrained designs.

faq.question: Can it replace a compiler or static analyzer?
faq.answer: No. Use compiler warnings, tests, clang-tidy, sanitizers, and Valgrind for verification.

faq.question: Does it cover multithreading?
faq.answer: Yes. It can reason about pthreads patterns, synchronization risks, and thread safety reviews.
